title: The Tight rope on the cart
subtitle: 工程建造 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 工程建造（科学与技术·工程与建造）
meta: 主题语境：工程建造（科学与技术·工程与建造）　|　核心词汇：tight　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 tight 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1978 the guide wrote of ① a tight rope on the cart in the guidebook, and everybody in the valley said at once that it was ② tighter than the one named there the year before. Three days on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the guide, who never explained anything, had done it year after year and gone home; it was the tight ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the tightest rope on the cart anybody in the valley had ever seen, or so the guidebook for July 1972 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too tight to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the traveller who had come to help; the tight ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the map at the far ledge, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a tight rule of the school, and said that no traveller in his right mind would call it ⑥ as tight as the rule of the school they had once had in the old valley. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was tight or not, and he said so.

By 1985 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the guidebook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something tight, and nothing besides. The traveller from the next valley called the whole plan ⑧ quite tight; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the guidebook kept the names of the tight ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1988, for the whole place, she wrote of another tight rope on the cart in the same guidebook, and the work, which took two days, seemed ⑨ tighter than anybody had expected. ⑩ The tightest rule of the school in the whole valley, she said in 1990, was the one she could never quite name; the tight ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 紧（前置定语 a tight rope on the cart：1978 年向导在旅行手册里记下的那件紧的绳子）
B. adj. 紧／严密（比较级 tighter than：文中两处，一处比车上绷紧的绳子，一处比预想）
C. adj. 紧／严密（最高级 the tightest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 紧（表语 too tight to do：母亲觉得它太紧，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 严密（前置定语 a tight rule of the school：叔叔把整件事称作一桩严密的规矩）
F. adj. 严密（同级比较 as tight as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩学校严密的规矩相比）
G. adj. 严密（后置定语 something tight：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 严密（受程度副词修饰 quite tight：那位旅人的评价）

items.q: a tight rope on the cart
the tightest rope on the cart anybody
a tight rule of the school
The tightest rule of the school in

answers.why: tight 意为“紧”，1978 年向导在旅行手册里记下的是“一件紧的绳子”，此处作前置定语 a tight rope on the cart。
tight 意为“紧”，此处用比较级 tighter than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
tight 意为“紧”，旅行手册上 七月 那行字说它是山谷里最紧的一件，故用最高级 the tightest rope on the cart。
tight 意为“紧”，母亲认为这件东西“太紧了，谁也用不上”，too tight to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
tight 意为“严密”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩严密的规矩”，此处作前置定语 a tight rule of the school。
tight 意为“严密”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩学校严密的规矩一样严密”，同级比较用 as tight as。
tight 意为“严密”，旅行手册上那半行字要的是“严密的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something tight。
tight 意为“严密”，邻山谷来的那位旅人认为这套计划“相当严密”，quite 修饰原级 tight。
tight 意为“严密”，1988 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要严密”，故用比较级 tighter than。
tight 意为“严密”，母亲 1990 年说的是“整个山谷里最严密的那一桩”，故用最高级 the tightest rule of the school。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1978 年，向导在旅行手册里记下了一件紧的绳子。（a tight rope on the cart）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更紧。（tighter than …）
母亲觉得它太紧，谁也用不上。（too tight to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩严密的规矩。（a tight rule of the school）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩学校严密的规矩一样严密。（as tight as …）
到了 1985 年，旅行手册上只剩半行字：要的是一件严密的东西。（something tight）
answers: In 1978 the guide wrote of a tight rope on the cart in the guidebook.
Everybody said it was tighter than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too tight to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a tight rule of the school.
He said nobody would call it as tight as the rule of the school they had once had.
By 1985 the guidebook asked for nothing but something tight.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 tight 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1978 the guide wrote of a tight rope on the cart in the guidebook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the tightest rope on the cart in the valley, or so the guidebook says.
My mother thought it too tight to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a tight rule of the school, and nobody argued with him.
The traveller from the next valley called the plan quite tight, and everybody laughed.
The tight ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
